overview: Physicists study how matter and energy behave, from particles to planets. Most of the work is research: designing experiments, running simulations, analyzing data and writing papers for scientific journals. O*NET rates science at 4.88 out of 5 for this job and mathematics at 4.5, and its investigative interest score is a maximum 7.00. Training is long, with 49% holding a doctoral degree and 39% post-doctoral training. In return, the BLS May 2025 median is $172,250. The job suits people who enjoy working independently on hard problems at a steady pace.
pay: Physicists earn a median of $172,250, and the top 10% earn $274,110 or more. Florida has the highest state median at $225,390, 31% above the national figure. California has by far the most jobs, 5,930, with a median of $207,490, and many of them are in federal research labs and technology companies.

faq.a: The BLS May 2025 median is $172,250 a year. The middle half earn between $111,720 and $222,760, and the lowest 10% earn under $82,110. Pay is highest in Florida, New Hampshire and Pennsylvania, where state medians are $210,990 or more, mostly in research and defense work.

faq.q: What degree do you need to be a physicist?
faq.a: Most research jobs need a PhD. In O*NET data, 49% of physicists hold a doctoral degree and 39% have post-doctoral training on top of it. There are 12 related majors, including physics, applied physics and astrophysics, and a bachelor's degree alone usually leads to technician or teaching roles.

Most physicists analyze research data, run complex calculations and report results in scientific papers. Some design instruments or work on lasers, semiconductors and medical imaging. O*NET rates knowledge of physics at 4.93 out of 5 and computers and electronics at 4.07, so coding is part of the daily work.

faq.q: What jobs are similar to physicist?
faq.a: The closest career changes are Mathematicians (81%), Biochemists and Biophysicists (79%) and Computer and Information Research Scientists (79%), based on O*NET 31.0. Computer Hardware Engineers are 74% matched and earn $161,740, which is 6% less than physicists, so research skills carry over well.
